questions.prompt: Organic chemistry is the study of carbon-based compounds.
questions.explanation: Organic chemistry is the study of carbon-based compounds, which are fundamental to life.

questions.prompt: The study of organic molecules is not useful in medicine or materials science.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The study of organic molecules is important for medicine, materials science and environmental science.

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon contains carbon and hydrogen only.
questions.explanation: A hydrocarbon is a compound that contains carbon and hydrogen only.

questions.prompt: Alcohols and esters are hydrocarbons because they contain carbon and hydrogen.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The three hydrocarbon families in this unit are alkanes, alkenes and alkynes.

questions.prompt: A functional group is an atom or group of atoms that decides the class of an organic compound.
questions.explanation: All compounds with the same functional group belong to the same class.

questions.prompt: The functional group of carboxylic acids is the carboxyl group, –COOH.
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl group –COOH.

questions.prompt: The general formula of an ester is RCOOR′.
questions.explanation: An ester has the general formula RCOOR′; R and R′ may be the same or different.

questions.prompt: The functional group of alcohols is the carboxyl group.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The functional group of alcohols is the hydroxyl group, –OH.

questions.prompt: The functional group present in esters is the hydroxyl group.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The functional group of esters is –COO–.

questions.prompt: The general formula of a carboxylic acid is RCOOR′.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The general formula of a carboxylic acid is RCOOH.

questions.prompt: A structural formula shows how the different atoms are joined up or arranged in a molecule.
questions.explanation: A structural formula shows how the atoms are joined up or arranged in a molecule or compound.

questions.prompt: A structural formula can be drawn in only one way.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: A structural formula can be written as a displayed formula or as a condensed formula.

questions.prompt: A displayed formula shows all the bonds between atoms as individual lines.
questions.explanation: A displayed formula shows all the bonds between the atoms as individual lines.

questions.prompt: In a displayed formula a triple bond is drawn as three lines.
questions.explanation: Three lines show a triple bond (C≡C).

questions.prompt: A displayed formula is drawn with the molecule straightened out and flattened.
questions.explanation: The molecule is straightened out and flattened to show exactly how all the atoms are joined.

questions.prompt: In a displayed formula a double bond is drawn as one line.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: In a displayed formula a double bond is drawn as two lines.

questions.prompt: A displayed formula is quick and easy to draw for every compound.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The drawback of a displayed formula is that it is very large and time-consuming to draw.

questions.prompt: The –CH₃ group is called the methyl group.
questions.explanation: –CH₃ is the methyl group and –CH₂– is the methylene group.

questions.prompt: Condensed formulae are more concise, while displayed formulae show clearly how atoms are connected.
questions.explanation: Displayed formulae give a clear view of connections; condensed formulae are more concise.

questions.prompt: A condensed formula shows every single bond as a separate line.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: A condensed formula groups the atoms joined to the same carbon, for example CH₃CH₃.

questions.prompt: The –CH₂– group is called the methyl group.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The –CH₂– group is called the methylene group.

questions.prompt: A hydrogen atom forms one bond.
questions.explanation: In structural formulae C = 4 lines, O = 2 lines and H = 1 line.

questions.prompt: Carbon 3 of butan-2-ol is bonded directly to 2 hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: In butan-2-ol (CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃) carbon 3 has 2 H.

questions.prompt: Carbon 5 of pent-1-ene is bonded directly to 3 hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: In pent-1-ene (CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂CH₃) carbon 5 has 3 H.

questions.prompt: Carbon 1 of pent-1-yne is bonded directly to 1 hydrogen atom.
questions.explanation: In pent-1-yne (CH≡CCH₂CH₂CH₃) carbon 1 has 1 H.

questions.prompt: Carbon 5 of pent-2-yne is bonded directly to 3 hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: In pent-2-yne (CH₃C≡CCH₂CH₃) carbon 5 has 3 H.

questions.prompt: Carbon 1 of propan-1-ol is bonded directly to 2 hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: In propan-1-ol (CH₃CH₂CH₂OH) carbon 1 has 2 H.

questions.prompt: Carbon 5 of pent-2-ene is bonded directly to 3 hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: In pent-2-ene (CH₃CH=CHCH₂CH₃) carbon 5 has 3 H.

questions.prompt: Each carbon atom in an organic compound forms three bonds.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: Each carbon atom in an organic compound forms four bonds.

questions.prompt: An oxygen atom forms four bonds.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: An oxygen atom forms two bonds.

questions.prompt: Carbon 2 of but-2-ene is bonded directly to 2 hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: False. in but-2-ene (CH₃CH=CHCH₃) carbon 2 has 1 H (four bonds in total).

questions.prompt: Carbon 1 of but-2-ene is bonded directly to 2 hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: False. in but-2-ene (CH₃CH=CHCH₃) carbon 1 has 3 H (four bonds in total).

questions.prompt: Carbon 1 of pentan-1-ol is bonded directly to 3 hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: False. in pentan-1-ol (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂OH) carbon 1 has 2 H (four bonds in total).

questions.prompt: Carbon 4 of pent-1-yne is bonded directly to 3 hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: False. in pent-1-yne (CH≡CCH₂CH₂CH₃) carbon 4 has 2 H (four bonds in total).

questions.prompt: The stems for 1, 2, 3 and 4 carbons are meth, eth, prop and but.
questions.explanation: Remember “Mice Eat Peanut Butter” = meth, eth, prop, but.

questions.prompt: The stem hex means six carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: Hexagon has 6 sides, so hex = 6.

questions.prompt: The stem oct means eight carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: Octagon has 8 sides, so oct = 8.

questions.prompt: The stem dec means ten carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: Decagon has 10 sides, so dec = 10.

questions.prompt: The stem hex means five carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The stem pent means five carbon atoms.

questions.prompt: The stem oct means seven carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The stem hept means seven carbon atoms.

questions.prompt: The stem dec means nine carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The stem non means nine carbon atoms.

questions.prompt: The stem “prop” means 4 carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: False. prop = 3 carbons.

questions.prompt: Alkenes have names ending in -ene.
questions.explanation: Alkene = C=C = -ene.

questions.prompt: Alcohols have names ending in -ol.
questions.explanation: The final “e” of the alkane name is replaced by “ol”.

questions.prompt: Ester names have the form alkyl … -oate.
questions.explanation: First word from the alcohol (-yl), second word from the acid (-oate).

questions.prompt: Alkanes have names ending in -ene.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: Alkanes have names ending in -ane.

questions.prompt: Alkynes have names ending in -ene.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: Alkynes have names ending in -yne.

questions.prompt: Carboxylic acids have names ending in -ol.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: Carboxylic acids have names ending in -oic acid.

questions.prompt: The memory trick a – e – y = 1 – 2 – 3 links -ane to a triple bond.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The memory trick a – e – y = 1 – 2 – 3 links -ane, -ene and -yne to single, double and triple bonds.

questions.prompt: The IUPAC system gives standard rules based on structure, avoiding the confusion of common names.
questions.explanation: IUPAC names are based on structure and avoid the confusion caused by common names.

questions.prompt: The stem tells the number of carbon atoms in the longest chain.
questions.explanation: meth = 1, eth = 2, prop = 3, but = 4, and so on.

questions.prompt: IUPAC stands for International Union of Physical and Applied Chemistry.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: IUPAC stands for International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry.

questions.prompt: Every organic name is made of a stem and a number only.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: Every organic name is made of a stem and a suffix.

questions.prompt: The suffix shows the number of carbon atoms.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The suffix shows the functional group (family) of the compound.

questions.prompt: The four-carbon alkane is butane.
questions.explanation: but + ane = butane, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₄H₁₀).

questions.prompt: The stem meth plus the ending -ane gives ethane.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: Stem meth plus ending -ane gives methane.

questions.prompt: In alkanes all the carbon atoms are joined to each other by single covalent bonds.
questions.explanation: All C–C bonds in an alkane are single bonds.

questions.prompt: The general formula of alkanes is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
questions.explanation: Butane C₄H₁₀ has 2 × 4 + 2 = 10 hydrogen atoms.

questions.prompt: Each middle carbon of an unbranched alkane carries two hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: A middle carbon has two C–C bonds and two C–H bonds.

questions.prompt: CH₃(CH₂)₃CH₃ is a shorter way of writing the condensed formula of pentane.
questions.explanation: CH₃(CH₂)₃CH₃ means CH₃, three CH₂ groups, then CH₃: five carbons, so pentane.

questions.prompt: CH₃(CH₂)₈CH₃ is decane.
questions.explanation: CH₃ + eight CH₂ + CH₃ = ten carbons, so decane (C₁₀H₂₂).

questions.prompt: The condensed structural formula of pentane is CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃.
questions.explanation: Pentane: pent = 5 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃ (C₅H₁₂).

questions.prompt: One molecule of ethane contains 6 hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: Ethane: eth = 2 carbons and -ane = only single bonds, so CH₃CH₃ (C₂H₆).

questions.explanation: False. ethyl ethanoate is an ester, which has the –COO– (ester) group.

questions.prompt: The smaller-number rule is used for alkenes, alkynes and alcohols.
questions.explanation: For alcohols the carbon bearing –OH gets the smaller number. For acids the –COOH carbon is always C-1.

questions.prompt: The 2 in pent-2-ene shows that the double bond starts on carbon number 2.
questions.explanation: It shows that the double bond starts on carbon 2 of the five-carbon chain.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in -ene is an alkene.
questions.explanation: The ending -ene shows a C=C double bond.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in -ol is an alcohol.
questions.explanation: The ending -ol shows the –OH group.

questions.prompt: A compound named alkyl … -oate is an ester.
questions.explanation: Esters are named alkyl … -oate, e.g. methyl ethanoate.

questions.prompt: An alcohol can be recognised by an –OH group attached to a carbon chain (R–OH).
questions.explanation: An alcohol is R–OH.

questions.prompt: CH₃CH₂CH₃ is an alkane because all its carbon–carbon bonds are single bonds.
questions.explanation: No double bond, triple bond or functional group = alkane.

questions.prompt: “Mice Eat Peanut Butter” stands for meth, eth, prop, but.
questions.explanation: M-E-P-B = meth, eth, prop, but.

questions.prompt: To draw a formula from a name: stem, suffix, place the group, then add hydrogens until every carbon has four bonds.
questions.explanation: ① stem, ② suffix, ③ number and place the double bond / triple bond / –OH / –COOH, ④ add hydrogens.

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon with the molecular formula C₃H₈ fits the general formula of the alkanes.
questions.explanation: C₃H₈ fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

questions.prompt: Hex-1-yne and hex-2-yne have the same molecular formula.
questions.explanation: Both are C₆H₁₀ but their structures differ.

questions.prompt: CH₃CH₂CH₂C≡CH is correctly named pent-1-yne.
questions.explanation: Number from the end that gives the smaller number: pent-1-yne.

questions.prompt: The displayed formula of methane has 4 C–H bonds.
questions.explanation: One C–H bond per hydrogen: 4.

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon with the molecular formula C₆H₁₀ fits the general formula of the alkynes.
questions.explanation: C₆H₁₀ fits CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon with the molecular formula C₃H₄ fits the general formula of the alkynes.
questions.explanation: C₃H₄ fits CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.

questions.prompt: The displayed formula of butane has 10 C–H bonds.
questions.explanation: One C–H bond per hydrogen: 10.

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon with the molecular formula C₃H₆ fits the general formula of the alkenes.
questions.explanation: C₃H₆ fits CₙH₂ₙ.

questions.prompt: The chain is always numbered from the left-hand end.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The chain is numbered from the end that gives the smaller number to the double bond.

questions.prompt: CH₃CH₂CH=CHCH₃ is correctly named pent-3-ene.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: CH₃CH₂CH=CHCH₃ is pent-2-ene because numbering from the right gives the smaller number.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in -ane is an alkene.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: A compound whose name ends in -ane is an alkane.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in -yne is an alkene.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: A compound whose name ends in -yne is an alkyne.

questions.prompt: A compound whose name ends in -oic acid is an ester.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: A compound whose name ends in -oic acid is a carboxylic acid.

questions.prompt: An ester can be recognised by an –OH group on a carbon chain.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: An ester can be recognised by the –COO– group between two carbon groups (RCOOR′).

questions.prompt: Two compounds with the same molecular formula must belong to the same family.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: Compounds with the same molecular formula can belong to different families, for example C₃H₆O₂.

questions.prompt: CH₃CH₂OH is a carboxylic acid because it contains an –OH group.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: CH₃CH₂OH is an alcohol because it has an –OH group attached to a carbon chain.

questions.prompt: The stems pent, hex and hept come from the shapes triangle, square and circle.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: The stems pent, hex, hept, oct, non, dec match the Greek numbers in pentagon, hexagon … decagon.

questions.prompt: After drawing a formula, count three bonds on every carbon.
questions.explanation: False. Correct statement: After drawing a formula, count four bonds on every carbon.

questions.prompt: The displayed formula of nonane has 19 C–H bonds.
questions.explanation: False. nonane has 20 hydrogens, so 20 C–H bonds.

questions.prompt: Hex-1-yne and hexane have the same molecular formula.
questions.explanation: False. hex-1-yne is C₆H₁₀ but hexane is C₆H₁₄.

questions.prompt: The displayed formula of ethane has 5 C–H bonds.
questions.explanation: False. ethane has 6 hydrogens, so 6 C–H bonds.

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon with the molecular formula C₂H₆ fits the general formula of the alkenes.
questions.explanation: False. C₂H₆ fits the general formula of the alkanes.
